questions.prompt: What is the radar equipment condition for navigating by radar?
answers: Approved, working radar or Inland ECDIS with radar overlay and required supporting equipment
questions.explanation: Article 4.06 specifies the working equipment for radar navigation.

questions.prompt: Who must be aboard for ordinary navigation by radar?
answers: A person with the specific radar authorization required by the authority
Any passenger who has used a plotter
questions.explanation: The authorized-person condition belongs to Article 4.06.

questions.prompt: When is the radar training exception available without that authorized person?
answers: Training in good visibility by day or night
questions.explanation: The exception is expressly for training in good visibility.

questions.prompt: What additional radio installation must a small craft using radar have?
questions.explanation: Article 4.06 separately addresses small craft using radar.

questions.prompt: If radar and Inland AIS simultaneously track the same target but disagree, what has the stated priority?
answers: The radar information for that target
The AIS symbol regardless of discrepancy
questions.explanation: Article 4.06(5) specifies radar information as the reliable one in this comparison.

questions.prompt: What does Inland AIS transmit to help identify traffic?
answers: Vessel data including position, course and navigational status
A live camera image of every vessel
A guarantee that all craft transmit
questions.explanation: Article 4.07 provides for vessel and dynamic data.

questions.prompt: If the vessel changes from under way to moored, what must happen to its AIS status?
answers: Update it to match the actual navigational status
questions.explanation: Article 4.07 requires current entered data.

questions.prompt: Does the ordinary Inland AIS carriage requirement cover every small craft?
answers: No; Article 4.07 states exceptions and a specific police craft qualification
Only if it has a white hull
questions.explanation: The provision states the equipment requirement and its exceptions.

questions.prompt: Before an equipped vessel enters a blind section, what radio action applies?
answers: Report on the allocated ship-to-ship channel
Call only after a collision risk appears
questions.explanation: Article 4.05 calls for reporting before entering specified blind sections.

questions.prompt: What should determine speed under reduced visibility?
answers: Visibility, traffic movements and local circumstances
The maximum speed indicated on the engine
questions.explanation: Article 6.30 calls for safe speed suited to conditions.

questions.prompt: A small craft under way in reduced visibility keeps which watch?
answers: Listening watch on the prescribed channel
Watch only on an entertainment radio
No radio watch if AIS is on
questions.explanation: The small-craft listening-watch provision is in Article 6.30.

questions.prompt: If you stop because of reduced visibility, where should you remain if possible?
questions.explanation: Article 6.30 directs vessels stopping to keep clear of the fairway where possible.

questions.prompt: An upstream vessel navigating by radar detects oncoming traffic. What is the next coordination step?
answers: Call by radiotelephone and agree the passing procedure
Rely only on a change of AIS colour
questions.explanation: Article 6.32 sets upstream radio coordination.

questions.prompt: What does a vessel without radar do in reduced visibility?
answers: Make for the nearest safe berth or anchorage under Article 6.33
Proceed normally to the planned destination
questions.explanation: Article 6.33 provides the safe-berth route.

questions.prompt: Which article sets formal reporting requirements for specified vessels at designated sectors?
questions.explanation: The sector reporting requirement is Article 8.02.

questions.prompt: When does a vessel subject to Article 8.02 report entry to a designated sector?
answers: As required before entering and again for sector entry and exit
Only after leaving the entire voyage
questions.explanation: The article covers advance reporting and sector entry and exit.

questions.prompt: What does sign B.11 relate to in this context?
questions.explanation: Article 4.05 identifies B.11 as a radio requirement.

questions.prompt: Who retains the navigation decision after information from radar, AIS and radio?
questions.explanation: Screen data informs but does not make the navigational decision.

questions.prompt: AIS shows no vessel around a bend but you cannot see into it. What is appropriate?
answers: Make the required ship-to-ship call and assess the blind approach
Treat empty AIS as a clear-water guarantee
questions.explanation: The blind-section report applies even if no AIS contact is shown.

questions.prompt: Your radar target is offset from its AIS position. How should you handle the target?
answers: Use radar as the reliable target tracking source and investigate the mismatch
questions.explanation: Article 4.06(5) addresses simultaneous radar and AIS tracking.

questions.prompt: The rate-of-turn indicator required for radar navigation has failed. What should you do?
answers: Do not continue navigating by radar as if Article 4.06 conditions are met
Assume AIS supplies the missing condition
questions.explanation: The required radar-navigation equipment must be in working order.

questions.prompt: You have no radar authorization aboard and fog closes in. Is the good-visibility training exception sufficient?
answers: No; do not rely on that exception for radar navigation in fog
Yes, the exception covers all weather
Yes if a phone is aboard
questions.explanation: The training exception is limited to good visibility.

questions.prompt: A small craft voluntarily uses AIS. Can its skipper treat that as a substitute for looking out?
answers: No; continue observation and radio practice required locally
Yes, AIS shows every craft and obstruction
questions.explanation: AIS cannot replace direct observation or the applicable radio provisions.

questions.prompt: Your AIS record still says under way after mooring. What is the operational correction?
answers: Leave the old status until tomorrow
questions.explanation: Article 4.07 requires the transmitted data to be current.

questions.prompt: You approach a bridge opening with poor sightlines and a working ship-to-ship radio. When should you report?
answers: Only if another AIS target appears
questions.explanation: Article 4.05 names bridge openings.

questions.prompt: A radar-equipped upstream vessel enters a sector where oncoming traffic may not yet appear on screen. What should it do?
answers: Make the Article 6.32 radiotelephone call and coordinate passing
Wait to transmit until after meeting
Assume no radar return means no traffic
questions.explanation: Article 6.32 includes sectors with unseen traffic.

questions.prompt: A downstream radar vessel detects a dangerous track with no radio contact. What is required first?
answers: Call attention to the danger by radio and agree a passing procedure
questions.explanation: The downstream provision is in Article 6.32.

questions.prompt: Visibility drops, and your craft is not navigating by radar. What is the route objective?
answers: Nearest safe berthing or anchoring area
The scheduled destination regardless of distance
questions.explanation: Article 6.33 specifies the nearest safe area.

questions.prompt: You must stop in fog. Which position is preferable?
answers: Outside the fairway as far as possible
questions.explanation: Article 6.30 addresses stopping positions.

questions.prompt: A reportable cargo vessel approaches a locally designated traffic-control sector. Which source determines the channel?
answers: The indicated channel and competent-authority instructions
questions.explanation: Article 8.02 uses the indicated reporting channel.

questions.prompt: A reportable vessel changes its reported cargo details during a designated sector. What should be done?
answers: Notify the competent authority promptly under Article 8.02
Wait for the voyage to end
Tell only another vessel on AIS
questions.explanation: Changes in reportable data must be notified.

questions.prompt: A reportable vessel interrupts its journey in a designated sector for over two hours. What is the reporting action?
answers: Report the beginning and end of the interruption
questions.explanation: Article 8.02 has an interruption reporting requirement.

questions.prompt: Which article contains the radar equipment and authorization conditions?
questions.explanation: Radar navigation conditions are in Article 4.06.

questions.prompt: What is an allowed radar display arrangement for navigation by radar under Article 4.06?
answers: Approved stand-alone radar or Inland ECDIS navigation mode with radar overlay
questions.explanation: Article 4.06 identifies the permitted radar arrangements.

questions.prompt: Which supporting instrument is ordinarily specified for navigating by radar?
answers: A compass rose painted on deck
questions.explanation: Article 4.06 requires a rate-of-turn indicator subject to stated exception.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the Article 4.06 good-visibility exception?
answers: Radar training without the authorized person aboard
questions.explanation: It applies to radar training in good visibility.

questions.prompt: A small craft navigating by radar also needs what?
questions.explanation: Article 4.06(4) states the radio condition.

questions.prompt: Which information is treated as the only reliable source for simultaneous radar and Inland AIS target tracking?
questions.explanation: Article 4.06(5) gives this target-tracking priority.

questions.prompt: Inland AIS position, course and status are primarily what?
answers: Transmitted vessel data used as part of the traffic picture
Proof that no untracked craft exist
questions.explanation: Article 4.07 concerns transmitted vessel data.

questions.prompt: How should entered Inland AIS data relate to the vessel?
answers: They must correspond to current actual particulars
They need only resemble a neighbouring vessel
questions.explanation: Article 4.07 requires accurate current entries.

questions.prompt: Which condition applies to small-craft AIS carriage under Article 4.07?
answers: There is an exception with a specified police-craft qualification
Every small craft must carry an Inland AIS transmitter
AIS is forbidden on every small craft
questions.explanation: The article distinguishes general carriage from small-craft exceptions.

questions.prompt: An equipped vessel approaches a designated blind section. When is its ship-to-ship report due?
answers: Only when a radar alarm sounds
questions.explanation: Article 4.05 sets the pre-entry report.

questions.prompt: What marks a competent authority radiotelephone requirement?
questions.explanation: Article 4.05 identifies sign B.11.

questions.prompt: What speed applies in reduced visibility?
answers: A safe speed adjusted to visibility and traffic
The normal open-water cruising speed without adjustment
The highest possible speed to leave fog
questions.explanation: Article 6.30 governs safe speed.

questions.prompt: What radio watch is specifically required of small craft under way in reduced visibility?
answers: Listening watch on the required ship-to-ship or prescribed channel
No listening watch if chartplotter is on
questions.explanation: Article 6.30 specifies the channel watch.

questions.prompt: Where should a vessel stopping because of reduced visibility remain if possible?
questions.explanation: Article 6.30 addresses stopping.

questions.prompt: Who should an upstream radar vessel contact after detecting oncoming traffic?
answers: No one if AIS is working
questions.explanation: Article 6.32 requires contact and passing coordination.

questions.prompt: What information accompanies an Article 6.32 upstream radar call?
questions.explanation: Article 6.32 lists these details.

questions.prompt: What does the downstream radar vessel do with a dangerous target lacking radio contact?
answers: Warn the target by radio and agree a passing procedure
questions.explanation: Article 6.32 directs the warning and coordination.

questions.prompt: Where must a vessel not navigating by radar in reduced visibility go?
answers: The furthest port on its schedule
questions.explanation: Article 6.33 sets the route objective.

questions.prompt: Which article governs formal vessel reporting at designated traffic sectors?
questions.explanation: Formal reporting is covered by Article 8.02.

questions.prompt: Are all pleasure craft automatically in the Article 8.02 reporting category list?
answers: No; check listed categories and any extra local requirements
questions.explanation: The article lists categories and allows competent-authority requirements.

questions.prompt: What are two routine sector messages for a vessel subject to Article 8.02?
questions.explanation: The sector entry and exit are reportable.

questions.prompt: How does a reportable vessel handle changed reportable data within a sector?
questions.explanation: Article 8.02 requires change notification.

questions.prompt: What duration of journey interruption triggers its specific Article 8.02 report?
answers: Only a pause longer than a week
questions.explanation: An interruption exceeding two hours has a reporting duty.

questions.prompt: When radar, AIS and the physical scene conflict, what should the boatmaster do?
answers: Resolve the discrepancy using the governing rules and safe navigation
Blindly follow whichever icon is nearest
questions.explanation: Sources must be interpreted against the applicable rules and conditions.
